comments.author: alter_igel
comments.why: Author cites own video as example of DIY microwave imaging.
comments.text: Author here. I agree with you, "full spectrum" is a generous marketing phrase for what might more accurately be called _extended_ spectrum. People way smarter than me have been able to achieve DIY spatial imaging with x-rays via compressed sensing [1] and with microwaves via phased arrays [2]. Optical wavelengths seem to be at a sweet spot of good angular resolution, varied natural sources, and harmless to humans. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]

comments.author: rubatuga
comments.story: WiFi Could Become an Invisible Mass Surveillance System
comments.why: Shows an ESP32 array localizing WiFi devices by phase and time.
comments.text: I was really impressed that a ESP32 Antenna Array Can essentially make a WiFi camera - it uses both time and phase differences to localize based on MAC addresses (which are sent plaintext) [VIDEO]

comments.why: Summarizes how ESP phase and amplitude data enable localisation.
comments.text: As shared elsewhere in this thread: [VIDEO] TL;DW: the ESP’s WiFi driver provides per incoming packet the carrier’s phase and amplitude. All ESPs are calibrated relatively to each other.
